offices.address: 320 S Jones Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89107, USA

about: High Stakes Injury Law is a personal injury firm with a single office in Las Vegas.

The firm states that it works on a contingency fee, with nothing to pay unless the case is won; the first consultation is free; its intake line is open around the clock. It publishes material in English and Spanish.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours and photo count come from the Places API. The owner's own description, the services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way. The API does expose Google's editorial summary, which is a different thing: Google writes those about notable places and has written one for no firm in this directory.

ahrefs.source: Ahrefs Site Explorer, batch endpoint, subdomains mode, organic figures for the United States

G1.evidence: Nevada does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.source: Published decisions of the Supreme Court of Nevada on the discipline of State Bar of Nevada members, indexed by CourtListener (Free Law Project)
G2.evidence: No attorney this firm names appears as the respondent in any of the 173 published discipline decisions of the Supreme Court of Nevada on the discipline of State Bar of Nevada members, 1992 to 2025. Published decisions record what has been decided, so this covers a disbarment or suspension on the record and not whether a registration is current today.

G3.evidence: 1 physical location verified on Google Business Profile. Nevada publishes no business register we are able to query, so the registration itself is not verified here. The state's own business search is the place to check it.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 2 named attorneys published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 922 public client reviews across 1 Google listing, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2023-05-01, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP

operating.source: Domain registration date over RDAP, which is a lower bound on how long the firm has been operating rather than its founding date

accountability.evidence: no bar or trial lawyers' association named on the pages we read · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

score.verdict: 3 of 5 eligibility gates passed. 2 could not be answered from the available records (G1, G3) and do not count against the firm. Strongest pillar: C; most headroom in pillar A (0/25).

subs.evidence: 922 Google reviews · Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

subs.label: Rating quality
subs.evidence: Google rating 4.7 over 922 reviews → Bayesian 4.71 (prior 4.83 weighted as 100 reviews, from 1184 scored firms) · single platform, Google only

subs.label: Review recency
subs.evidence: 5 of 5 sampled reviews are from the last 12 months (newest 2026-07-31) · a sample of five per business listing, not every review

subs.label: Complaint share
subs.evidence: 0 of 5 sampled reviews rate 1 or 2 stars · a sample, so this is the shape of the complaints rather than a count of them

subs.label: Website trust & experience
subs.evidence: CWV fail · no bar numbers on bios · no fee statement · privacy policy · disclaimer · fresh content

subs.label: Search authority
subs.evidence: DR 26 → 63th pct of 83-firm cohort (median 19) 2/3 · 1,025 referring domains, 45th pct 1/2 · 28 organic keywords / 138 visits·mo, 42th pct 1/2 · brand demand 0/1 (pending)

subs.label: Local presence
subs.evidence: 1 operational Google Business Profile listing · 10 or more photos, which is where the API stops counting · 5 categories, hours published, which almost every listing here has and so separates nobody · the services list, Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the Places API does not expose, and NAP consistency across citations and local-pack rank have no source here, so the rest of this sub-factor leaves the scale rather than being scored as unearned

subs.label: Content, E-E-A-T & schema
subs.evidence: JSON-LD detected 1/1 · not assessed on any firm yet, so content depth and earned media and AI citations leave the scale (4 pts)
